Q: How do citation spans, source versions and claim coverage make an answer auditable?
A: A citation should identify inspectable evidence supporting the associated claim, ideally with the source revision and relevant location. Merely listing related documents does not establish entailment. Split a multi-part answer into claims and check whether each supported claim has the necessary evidence and applicability context. Keep extraction and chunk identities linked to their source so a reader can verify the exact text that informed the answer. Unsupported claims need omission, qualification or an explicit request for more information.
Why: An answer states a 30-day deadline and a fee exemption but cites a passage supporting only the deadline. One valid citation does not support the additional exemption, even when both appear in the same sentence.
Risk: Citation formatting can make unsupported content appear trustworthy.
Trade: Finer evidence links improve auditability while requiring stable provenance and UI support.
Try: Mark the supported span for each claim in a two-clause answer and identify any unsupported clause.
